Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

startIf: No sharp pain in muscles or joints.
Breathing feels normal during the warmup jog.
Legs feel responsive during light stride checks.
modifyIf: Sleep was poor (under 6 hours) or hydration is low.

environmentAdjustments.road: Choose flat, traffic-free paths. Run on soft shoulders if available.
environmentAdjustments.treadmill: Use 1-2% incline to simulate wind resistance and match road effort.
environmentAdjustments.hotWeather: Reduce target speed by 5-10%. Extend recovery intervals as needed.

makeEasier: Reduce the total count of repetitions by 1-2.

sourceNote: Workout design informed by research on energy system demands, training distribution, and recovery best practices.

trainingPurpose.practicalUse: Develops maximum velocity, improves starting acceleration, and optimizes high-speed coordination.
trainingPurpose.notFor: Avoid if hamstring tightness or nerve entrapment is present.

executionCues: Focus on explosive force application during the acceleration phase.
Relax your face, jaw, and hands; tension restricts maximum velocity.
Maintain high knee drive and active hip extension.

startIf: No sharp pain in muscles or joints.
Breathing feels normal during the warmup jog.
Legs feel responsive during light stride checks.
modifyIf: Sleep was poor (under 6 hours) or hydration is low.
Muscles feel unusually stiff but no sharp pain.
Warmup feels sluggish.
skipIf: Sharp pain that causes limping or gait compensation.
Feeling dizzy, lightheaded, or having systemic symptoms.
Elevated resting heart rate indicating under-recovery.

environmentAdjustments.track: Use lanes consistently. Check direction rules to protect hips.
environmentAdjustments.road: Choose flat, traffic-free paths. Run on soft shoulders if available.
environmentAdjustments.treadmill: Use 1-2% incline to simulate wind resistance and match road effort.
environmentAdjustments.hotWeather: Reduce target speed by 5-10%. Extend recovery intervals as needed.
environmentAdjustments.hills: Maintain steady effort, not pace, when running uphill.

makeEasier: Reduce the total count of repetitions by 1-2.
Extend the recovery time by 30-60 seconds.
Run at a slightly more relaxed effort level.
makeHarder: Add 1-2 repetitions, maintaining the same target pace.
Slightly shorten recoveries or transition to an active float recovery.
Complete the final repeat slightly faster while maintaining form.
doNotProgressIf: Pace drops by more than 5% across intervals.
Form begins to break down or coordination is lost.
Persistent muscle tightness or sharp pain is felt.

riskReasons: Maximal speed reps create high force demands on the hamstrings and Achilles tendon.
Neuromuscular coordination drops rapidly under fatigue, increasing muscle strain risk.
riskProfile.saferAlternative: Complete repeats at 90% effort (controlled strides) rather than absolute 100% max velocity.

title: Elite Extended Speed Rhythm Reps
summary: Structured 200m workout focusing on speed, speed endurance.
riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 150m at target Near-maximal Sprint Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 300s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 3 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 3 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 6 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 6 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 300s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Curve running requires progressive inward lean and rapid arm action.
Maintain speed rhythm as you transition out of the curve onto the home straight.
Recovery walking should be slow and deliberate to allow lactate dispersion.
commonMistakes: Neglecting full recoveries, which compromises speed quality and increases risk of hamstring strain.
Overstriding (reaching too far forward with the heel), which acts as a brake.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 220m at target Near-maximal Sprint Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 4 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 4 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 8 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 8 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Curve running requires progressive inward lean and rapid arm action.
Maintain speed rhythm as you transition out of the curve onto the home straight.
Recovery walking should be slow and deliberate to allow lactate dispersion.
commonMistakes: Neglecting full recoveries, which compromises speed quality and increases risk of hamstring strain.
Overstriding (reaching too far forward with the heel), which acts as a brake.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

sourceNote: Workout design informed by research on energy system demands, training distribution, and recovery best practices.

trainingPurpose.practicalUse: Develops maximum velocity, improves starting acceleration, and optimizes high-speed coordination.
trainingPurpose.notFor: Avoid if hamstring tightness or nerve entrapment is present.

executionCues: Focus on explosive force application during the acceleration phase.
Relax your face, jaw, and hands; tension restricts maximum velocity.
Maintain high knee drive and active hip extension.

startIf: No sharp pain in muscles or joints.
Breathing feels normal during the warmup jog.
Legs feel responsive during light stride checks.
modifyIf: Sleep was poor (under 6 hours) or hydration is low.
Muscles feel unusually stiff but no sharp pain.
Warmup feels sluggish.
skipIf: Sharp pain that causes limping or gait compensation.
Feeling dizzy, lightheaded, or having systemic symptoms.
Elevated resting heart rate indicating under-recovery.

environmentAdjustments.track: Use lanes consistently. Check direction rules to protect hips.
environmentAdjustments.road: Choose flat, traffic-free paths. Run on soft shoulders if available.
environmentAdjustments.treadmill: Use 1-2% incline to simulate wind resistance and match road effort.
environmentAdjustments.hotWeather: Reduce target speed by 5-10%. Extend recovery intervals as needed.
environmentAdjustments.hills: Maintain steady effort, not pace, when running uphill.

makeEasier: Reduce the total count of repetitions by 1-2.
Extend the recovery time by 30-60 seconds.
Run at a slightly more relaxed effort level.
makeHarder: Add 1-2 repetitions, maintaining the same target pace.
Slightly shorten recoveries or transition to an active float recovery.
Complete the final repeat slightly faster while maintaining form.
doNotProgressIf: Pace drops by more than 5% across intervals.
Form begins to break down or coordination is lost.
Persistent muscle tightness or sharp pain is felt.

riskReasons: Maximal speed reps create high force demands on the hamstrings and Achilles tendon.
Neuromuscular coordination drops rapidly under fatigue, increasing muscle strain risk.
riskProfile.saferAlternative: Complete repeats at 90% effort (controlled strides) rather than absolute 100% max velocity.

sourceNote: Workout design informed by research on energy system demands, training distribution, and recovery best practices.

trainingPurpose.practicalUse: Develops maximum velocity, improves starting acceleration, and optimizes high-speed coordination.
trainingPurpose.notFor: Avoid if hamstring tightness or nerve entrapment is present.

executionCues: Focus on explosive force application during the acceleration phase.
Relax your face, jaw, and hands; tension restricts maximum velocity.
Maintain high knee drive and active hip extension.

startIf: No sharp pain in muscles or joints.
Breathing feels normal during the warmup jog.
Legs feel responsive during light stride checks.
modifyIf: Sleep was poor (under 6 hours) or hydration is low.
Muscles feel unusually stiff but no sharp pain.
Warmup feels sluggish.
skipIf: Sharp pain that causes limping or gait compensation.
Feeling dizzy, lightheaded, or having systemic symptoms.
Elevated resting heart rate indicating under-recovery.

environmentAdjustments.track: Use lanes consistently. Check direction rules to protect hips.
environmentAdjustments.road: Choose flat, traffic-free paths. Run on soft shoulders if available.
environmentAdjustments.treadmill: Use 1-2% incline to simulate wind resistance and match road effort.
environmentAdjustments.hotWeather: Reduce target speed by 5-10%. Extend recovery intervals as needed.
environmentAdjustments.hills: Maintain steady effort, not pace, when running uphill.

makeEasier: Reduce the total count of repetitions by 1-2.
Extend the recovery time by 30-60 seconds.
Run at a slightly more relaxed effort level.
makeHarder: Add 1-2 repetitions, maintaining the same target pace.
Slightly shorten recoveries or transition to an active float recovery.
Complete the final repeat slightly faster while maintaining form.
doNotProgressIf: Pace drops by more than 5% across intervals.
Form begins to break down or coordination is lost.
Persistent muscle tightness or sharp pain is felt.

riskReasons: Maximal speed reps create high force demands on the hamstrings and Achilles tendon.
Neuromuscular coordination drops rapidly under fatigue, increasing muscle strain risk.
riskProfile.saferAlternative: Complete repeats at 90% effort (controlled strides) rather than absolute 100% max velocity.

title: Systematic Speed Endurance Reps Session
summary: Structured 200m workout focusing on speed, speed endurance.
riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 80m at target Near-maximal Sprint Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 10 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 8 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 8 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 10 repeats.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 12 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 12 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 10 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Curve running requires progressive inward lean and rapid arm action.
Maintain speed rhythm as you transition out of the curve onto the home straight.
Recovery walking should be slow and deliberate to allow lactate dispersion.
commonMistakes: Neglecting full recoveries, which compromises speed quality and increases risk of hamstring strain.
Overstriding (reaching too far forward with the heel), which acts as a brake.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.
